report.summary: Reviewed the v4 optional-source-lead authority boundary read-only across the publication policy, contracts, strict export/verifier, human risk-review and repair APIs, the assessment UI, and the listed tests. Fallback ordering, active-risk/adjustment exclusion, original-order preservation, legacy v1–v3 import handling, the v4 namespace/reason repair rejection, and the component disclosure structure all check out on inspection. However, v4 exact-withheld human comments can name an unrelated valid criterion, and those comments then surface as linked repair work on that criterion via the existing riskSource linkage, which conflicts with the 'comments exact withheld origin only, no linked repair' requirement. I did not execute anything; findings rest on source reasoning.

findings.title: Withheld-origin human comment is not bound to its published criterion and seeds linked repair work on any ordinary criterion
findings.evidence: recordRiskReview accepts an input with riskOrigin:'withheld' when the pool is a valid v4 disposition (line 40-44 unbound, line 50 eligible) and checks only delivery, report, withheld entry and index (line 51). It never records or checks a criterionId, and ProofRiskReview (contracts.ts:101) has no criterion field. The review that is then saved is `{deliveryId, assessmentId, riskIndex, riskOrigin:'withheld', decision, reason, ...}` (line 60). The UI (DeliveryAssessment.tsx:207) renders this panel for every withheld entry, including v4, with the same onSaveRiskReview. By contrast, linked repair feedback is an ordinary ProofFeedback tied to `criterionId` plus `riskSource` ({assessmentId, riskIndex}) (contracts.ts:149, risk-repairs.ts:8-10). replayRiskRepairs resolves that pair only against the active published pool: `tasks.set(... source ...)` (risk-repairs.ts:84-88) never consults the withheld pool. So a criterionId with riskIndex 0/1 that is validated separately now means the v4 lead. Nothing prevents that after a human comment. The v4 publication notes say human opinions "do not release the gate". The non-scoped path has the same root cause. That is outside the v4-specific focus but shares this API.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace using tests/assessment-unbound-withholding.test.ts fixture(): fixture() returns active risks [] and withheldRisks {version:4, entries[0..1]}. Call recordRiskReview(q,'buyer',{deliveryId:d.id,assessmentId:a.id,riskIndex:0,riskOrigin:'withheld',decision:'confirmed',reason:'add this label'},at). It succeeds and saves a riskReview whose only lead identity is riskIndex 0. Next, call requestChanges(next,{deliveryId:d.id,feedback:[{criterionId:'manual-1',comment:'Add the E-mail label described above.',riskSource:{assessmentId:a.id,riskIndex:0}}]},at). snapshotRiskFeedbackSource rejects the same pair only while the marker is v4 (risk-repairs.ts:65), but requestChanges rebuilds the source from `report.risks[0]`. With active risks [] that fails closed today, so nothing is linked yet (noted as a limit below). The accepted human review still asserts that withheld lead 0 was confirmed against 'manual-1' without any recorded binding, and any later published/model-authored risk at index 0 would be treated as the same lead. The comment therefore carries no exact origin that a downstream consumer can verify.
findings.suggestion: Bind the human comment to the exact withheld record. Add an optional `withheldCriterionId` or `withheldLeadDigest` to ProofRiskReview and RiskReviewInput, make it required when riskOrigin==='withheld' (reject otherwise), and verify it against the pool entry and the same derived relation used at publication time. Alternatively, label v4-quality comments as origin-only with no criterion attribute at all, and exclude origin-only records from any path that correlates a criterionId with riskSource. Either way, add a test that a withheld comment cannot be turned into a requestChanges feedback for an arbitrary criterion.

limitations: Read-only review of only the supplied packet. No command, test, typecheck, build, SSR render, provider or network call was executed, so every claim is unexecuted source reasoning.

Several modules the behaviour depends on were not included: requestChanges in lib/proof-workflow.ts, AssessmentValidationPanel and RiskRepairPanel, RiskReviewPanel markup, lib/assessment-display.ts (assessmentRiskPresentation/assessmentReviewSummary), lib/delivery-assessment.ts (which builds the ObservationScopeContext and publication order), lib/business-checks.ts (getBusinessCheckPlan), lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts, assessment-limits.ts and static-resources.ts. Import-handling paths through those files, and exact publication-order assumptions, could not be verified.

The replay test's all3 reconstruction relies on fixture functions and a controlled fetch shim. That proves replay determinism and raw preservation only. It does not establish provider authenticity, fresh inference, or that the historical sourceHead bytes were unchanged; no historical corpus, freeze, or raw source was in the packet.
The separate old full-core historical replay, its publication-delta accounting, and the root-owned tooling regression are outside this packet and were not assessed.
Per the stated compatibility rule, a report-level v4 type was not inferred where a pool-less legacy report exists, and removed provenance was not treated as inferable.
